title: Restock a spring-pusher shelf lane behind the older stock, holding the pusher back
instruction: Pull the grey pusher back and hold it. Set both blue cartons in the lane behind the red ones, without passing either over the red ones, then let the pusher forward so it closes up the row.
context: Stock clerks refill spring-pusher lanes: the pusher is held back by hand while new stock goes in behind the old, so old stock stays at the front and is never passed over (O*NET 53-7065.00, Stockers and Order Fillers). Closest on the board: 'Reset a tripped breaker under a spring-shut cover' and 'Hold a lid open and retrieve an item' (hold open, then act), 'Hold a bag's pocket flap open and stow a charger inside' and 'Pull a red-tagged tote from a flow lane without letting the queue move more than 2 cm'; new here: the load on the held arm rises the further the pusher is held back, the released pusher closes the row up, and the order of the stock is scored.
setup: Positions are object centres in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. Table: oak top, arm bases 61 cm apart. Lane, fixed on the table along x at y 0: floor of off-white plastic, x 6.5 to 41, y -4.6 to +4.6, 0.8 cm thick; two dark rails of painted steel along its sides, 0.6 cm wide and 2.8 cm tall from the table's top surface (inner width 8 cm); a dark front wall of painted steel at x 5.5 to 6.5, y -4.6 to +4.6, 7 cm tall. Friction of the lane surfaces about 0.4. Old stock: two red cartons, 5 x 5 x 8 cm, 40 g, painted cardboard, standing on the floor with centres at x 9 and 14.1, y 0; the first touches the front wall and is about 1 mm from the second, and the second is about 1 mm from the pusher plate. Pusher: a grey sprung slide of painted steel with a plate x 16.7 to 17.7, y +-3.9, z 1 to 5.5 cm above the table, joined at its back face to a rigid side arm (grey, x 17.7 to 18.9, y -3.9 to -17, z 3 to 4.5 cm above the table, passing above the right rail's 2.8 cm top) that ends in a light grey handle x 18.2 to 21.2, y -13 to -17, z 3 to 7.5 cm above the table; the handle is offset to y -15 so the right arm works outside the left arm's area, and everything is below the 8.8 cm carton tops. It slides along x on a drawer slide (0 to 20 cm back from its rest mark, 0 = plate about 1 mm behind the second red carton) and a linear spring pulls it forward, 2.9 N at 19 cm back (15 N/m), with damping of 10 N s/m (a real lane gets this from a soft-close damper on the drawer slide); the pusher weighs 50 g. New stock: two blue cartons, 5 x 5 x 8 cm, 40 g, painted cardboard, standing on the table at (15, 20) and (25, 20).
scoring: J = pusher's distance from its rest mark (ruler). In the lane: outline inside the rails and front wall (touching or within 2 mm past counts), bottom within 1 cm of the floor (carton top at most 9.8 cm above the table), tilt at most 10 degrees (top edge within 1.4 cm sideways of the bottom edge), back face at most 4 mm past the plate face. 0: a blue carton ever over the reds' place (x 5.5 to 16.6, y -4.6 to +4.6 cm, any height; under 3 mm is contact), or a blue in the lane nearer the front wall than a red, or a red not in the lane. 1.0: all four in the lane, J 9.2 to 11.0 cm, all still (under 1 cm/s), held 4 s or to the last step. 0.75: all four in the lane otherwise. 0.5: both reds and one blue in the lane. 0.25: pusher 6 cm or more back for 1 s with both reds in the lane within 1 cm of start. Else 0. Cameras: top, above x 16.6, y 0, 1 m up; side, table height, 1 m left.
reset_notes: Stand the red cartons against the front wall, the second red about 1 mm from the pusher plate (the pusher rests on its stop; it is not pressed against the red), and the blue cartons at their marks on the table. The lane stays fixed.
fidelity: Approximate. The side-arm handle is simplified (a real one has a tab on its plate). The pusher is a drawer-slide joint with a linear spring and damping (a real one uses a constant-force spring). Cartons are rigid boxes. The simulator scores the final step with grippers closed, so score() counts a carton whose bottom is more than 1 cm above every support as not placed, and a blue carton over the red cartons' place at any height as a violation.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (right arm reached the pusher handle, blue cartons stayed on the table); demo: 1.0 (right arm held pusher back, left arm set both blue cartons behind the reds)
